cells.tense: You're here, finishing something, and you can feel what's next pulling at you.
cells.verb: feeling the pull of all the things your heart could go toward
cells.place: at the place where a thing is done and lets you go on
cells.ask: If you want it: look at what's pulling you and find the shape that runs through it — not to pick, just to see what kind of thing you keep being drawn to. The pulls get clearer, and you stay yourself inside them.
cells.core:
You're here, finishing something, and you can feel what's next pulling at you — more than one thing, and none of them frightening. That's not restlessness. An ending that's really done makes room, and the room fills with what you might want, and you can feel all of it without grabbing. You're drawn and still standing where you are.

If you want it: look at what's pulling you and find the shape that runs through it. Not to pick, just to see what kind of thing you keep being drawn to. The pulls get clearer, and you stay yourself inside them.
cells.sheetLine: You finish, and you can feel what's next without grabbing at it.

cells.tense: You're already in the next thing before this one has closed.
cells.verb: feeling the pull of everything you could want at once
cells.place: at the place where a thing should be done and isn't
cells.ask: Pick one thing that's actually finished and let it stay finished — put it down as made, no reopening, for a week. The pulls don't vanish; they stop running you. You can feel a wanting and not become it.
cells.core:
You're already in the next thing before this one has closed. Every time something finishes, ten new wants show up in the open space, and you're off toward them — so nothing ever gets to be done, it just gets left. Somewhere ahead is a version of you who has felt all of it, and you're living there instead of here.

Pick one thing that's actually finished and let it stay finished. Put it down as made, no reopening, for a week. The pulls don't vanish; they stop running you. You can feel a wanting and not become it.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing gets to be done because everything after it is already pulling.

cells.tense: Something is finished and you're still standing where it finished.
cells.verb: feeling almost nothing pull you forward
cells.place: at a door that's already behind you
cells.ask: Don't try to make yourself want things. Instead, sit still with what's done until your mind goes quiet about it — no sorting, no deciding, just settled. The pull comes back on its own, and you're there to feel it without losing yourself in it.
cells.core:
Something is finished and you're still standing where it finished. The door closed and nothing pulled you through to the next one, so you stayed — and somewhere in the staying you stopped expecting to feel the pull at all. It's not that there's nothing to want. It's that the wanting has gone flat and you've been calling that peace.

Don't try to make yourself want things. Instead, sit still with what's done until your mind goes quiet about it — no sorting, no deciding, just settled. The pull comes back on its own, and you're there to feel it without losing yourself in it.
cells.sheetLine: The thing is done and nothing pulled you on, so you stayed.

cells.tense: You're being drawn somewhere right now and you'd say you're just drifting.
cells.verb: being pulled toward what you want to feel
cells.place: at the place where one thing closes and the next one opens
cells.ask: Take the last three things you reached for after something ended and say plainly what they have in common. One pattern, in your own words. The pull gets a name and an owner, and you can feel it fully without being swept.
cells.core:
You're being drawn somewhere right now and you'd say you're just drifting. Every time something finishes, you turn toward one thing and not another — a person, a project, a feeling — and you talk about it like the wind did it. But the turning has a direction, and the direction is yours. The wanting is steering; you've just taken your hands off it.

Take the last three things you reached for after something ended and say plainly what they have in common. One pattern, in your own words. The pull gets a name and an owner, and you can feel it fully without being swept.
cells.sheetLine: You keep being drawn the same direction. You call it chance.
